rule.borderline_note: Rows flagged borderline are the ones where the two readings genuinely compete. Every one carries the reasoning that decided it, so a human can flip it and rerun.
rule.not_scheme: the money runs, builds, staffs or maintains an organisation or an asset, devolves general purpose funds to another tier of government, pays for the capacity of the delivery system rather than the benefit, discharges the state's obligation to its own serving or retired staff, or is an accounting or adjustment head
rule.scheme: the money buys an identifiable benefit received by a person or household: cash, a kit, food, a scholarship, a fee waiver, a pension, insurance, a subsidy, a loan, free travel, free power, a house, treatment for a named beneficiary class, or training in which the trainee is himself the beneficiary class
rule.the_line_that_did_the_work: Two lines did most of the work in Tamil Nadu and neither appears in Karnataka or Andhra Pradesh. First, an employment obligation is not a welfare scheme: the service pension, the family pension, the death gratuity, the medical allowance to pensioners, the house building advance and the funeral assistance to the state's own anganwadi and noon meal workers are all payments to identifiable households and all of them are labelled not_scheme, because the state is paying them as an employer. The social pensions under major head 2235 are schemes; the service pensions under major head 2071 are not, and the two are printed in the same words with the same object head 327. Second, for the central crop missions the state's own object head decides: booked as 311 Subsidies the money is paid out to the grower and the row is a scheme, booked as 309 Grants-in-Aid it goes to an implementing agency and the row is not.

sampling: Stratified by department family (WELFARE, SERVICE, ECONOMY, INFRA, GOVERNANCE, a fixed partition of the 55 demand books listed in parse/classify_tamilnadu.py) crossed with allocation band (nil, and quartiles of the 4,632 heads that carry an allocation), 25 non-empty strata. The 55 books cannot each be a stratum: 55 books crossed with 5 bands is 275 cells and a sample large enough to fill them could not be labelled by hand. Within a stratum rows are sorted by head of account and picked at even spacing, so the sample is reproducible without a random seed. Allocation is proportional to stratum size with a floor of 6, so the sample is close to self weighting; stratum_size and stratum_sampled are carried on every stratified row so a weighted estimate can be recomputed.

audit.what: Every row the classifier scores 8 or above that the stratified sample had not already covered. Together the two sets are a census of the published region and of the band immediately below it, so the published list's precision is counted rather than estimated. The audit was made after the weights were fixed and was not fed back into them.

stratified.what: A probability sample of all 6,220 heads of account, stratified by department family crossed with allocation band. This is the only set the threshold sweep uses, because precision and recall estimated on anything else would not generalise to the rows the classifier has not seen.

what: Hand labels for Tamil Nadu's Demand Book sub-heads, a stratified probability sample plus an audit census of everything the classifier scores at or above 8. Ground truth for parse/classify_tamilnadu.py. Audit and correct these: the classifier is only as good as they are.
